subject: Custom runtime skinning & governance — POC scope
messages:
From: Nate Green <nate@avasolutions.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.s@avasolutions.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Custom runtime skinning & governance — POC scope

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for taking time on the call yesterday. As discussed, Ava Solutions is exploring a small POC to embed a Redwood runtime into our analytics product so customers can white‑label the assistant UI and push branding/styling and a limited governance layer (policy hooks + simple audit events) back to our control plane.

High level asks for the POC:
- A lightweight skinnable runtime that can accept CSS/UX tokens and a brand identifier.
- Governance hooks for request/response filtering and audit event emission to our collector.
- A short SLA for uptime during the POC window and a security checklist (SOC2 items).
- A rough commercial frame: one year ISV license + dev support.

Attached a one‑page summary (redwood_skinning_poc_scope.pdf) and our brand guidelines excerpt. Could you confirm feasibility and any gating items (legal, performance, data paths)?

Cheers,
Nate
Nate Green | Head of Product, Ava Solutions
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Nate Green <nate@avasolutions.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom runtime skinning & governance — POC scope

Hi Nate — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick thoughts:
- Feasible: our runtime can be configured to accept styling tokens and a brand id; we can mirror CSS tokens to a restricted set of UX primitives (colors, fonts, avatar).
- Governance: we already support request/response middleware (can run pre/post processors). We need to agree on the exact hooks and whether Ava's collector receives raw events or anonymized telemetry.
- Security: happy to run through the SOC2 checklist. We'll share a trimmed security pack for POC.

I looped in Karthik (product) and Marissa (sales/partner ops) to scope out technical and commercial guardrails. Can we schedule a 45‑minute POC scoping call next week? Options: Tue 11/9 11:00am PT or Wed 11/10 2:00pm PT.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Suresh <priya.s@avasolutions.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom runtime skinning & governance — POC scope

Hi all — thanks, Hannah. We prefer Wed 11/10 at 2pm PT. A few clarifying items for the agenda so the call is productive:
- Example flow: customer launches a white‑labeled assistant inside Ava; we pass brand id in auth token, Redwood serves model responses; Ava should receive audit events with (redacted) user intent + timestamps.
- Security: does Redwood require inbound connections to your control plane for telemetry, or can we push events out to our collector? We need to avoid any inbound firewall openings for our enterprise customers.
- Performance: target tail latency under 400ms p50 for 1–2 concurrent sessions per tenant during POC. If there are special kernel/quantization options we should enable, please note.
- Commercial: we expect a one‑time POC engineering credit and then an annual ISV fee — will Redwood provide a POC estimate?

Attaching the brand snippet (skin-branding-guidelines.png) for the UI team.

Thanks,
Priya
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Suresh <priya.s@avasolutions.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom runtime skinning & governance — POC scope

Priya — appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers ahead of the 11/10 call:
- Telemetry: we can support push model only — Redwood will emit structured audit events to a webhook endpoint you control (no inbound connections required). Events can be configured to omit or hash PII.
- Hooks: we can surface a pre‑processor hook (sync) for allow/deny decisions, and a post‑processor (async) for enriched telemetry. Pre‑processor will add ~5–15ms overhead depending on the logic you run.
- Skinning: we will accept a sealed theme payload (JSON) that maps to an allowlisted set of UI tokens. We will not render arbitrary CSS; this reduces XSS surface for customers.
- Latency: 400ms p50 is reasonable in the Dedicated/hosted tier for the POC; we'll instrument targeted profiling and surface p50/p95. For POC we'll propose a small dedicated pool with 2 vGPU instances.
- Commercial: Marissa — can you propose a POC fee (engineering credit) + annual ISV anchor price? We'll aim to keep POC scope contained.

Connor — can you prepare a short security pack (SOC2 highlights + a minimal SLA) and attach a draft SLA doc?

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Suresh <priya.s@avasolutions.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom runtime skinning & governance — POC scope

Thanks everyone — great sync today. Follow ups and next steps (action items):

1) POC deliverables (estimated 6 weeks):
   - Technical: theme payload integration, pre/post hook implementation, webhook for audit events, profiling and perf dashboard.
   - Security/compliance: Redwood security pack + signed minimal SLA (attached: security-sla-draft.docx).
   - Business: one month POC credit (50% off standard ISV onboarding) + proposed annual ISV list price (attached in HubSpot note).

2) Open questions for legal/ops:
   - IP: who owns theme assets and whether it's allowed to persist brand token mapping in logs. Recommend we add an explicit clause in the MPA about non‑storage of raw PII.
   - Support: define severity levels for POC and response times.

3) Next meetings:
   - Legal sync: Tue 11/16 9:00am PT (Hannah, Marissa, Ava legal)
   - Engineering kickoff: Mon 11/22 10:00am PT (Redwood eng + Ava eng)

Attachments referenced: redwood_skinning_poc_scope.pdf, skin-branding-guidelines.png, security-sla-draft.docx.

I'll add the HubSpot deal note and send DocuSign for the POC MPA template after legal confirms.

— Marissa
